outline.chapter_title: Introduction to Mathematical Reasoning with Large Language Models
outline.description: Sets the stage by explaining why mathematical reasoning is challenging for LLMs, reviewing prior work, and motivating the DeepSeekMath project.
subtopics: Limitations of existing open‑source models
Benchmark landscape (GSM8K, MATH, CMATH, etc.)
Goals of DeepSeekMath: performance, openness, and scalability
Overview of the DeepSeekMath system architecture

outline.chapter_title: Building a Large‑Scale Math Corpus from the Web
outline.description: Describes the data collection pipeline that creates the 120 B‑token DeepSeekMath Corpus, including filtering, de‑duplication, and multilingual considerations.
subtopics: Seed corpus selection (OpenWebMath) and fastText classifier training
Iterative mining and domain‑level expansion
URL‑based deduplication and near‑deduplication techniques
Human annotation loop and classifier re‑training
De‑contamination to avoid benchmark leakage
Multilingual content and token statistics

outline.chapter_title: Evaluating Corpus Quality and Comparative Analysis
outline.description: Presents experiments that compare the DeepSeekMath Corpus against other math corpora and explain how quality is measured.
subtopics: Baselines: MathPile, OpenWebMath, Proof‑Pile‑2
Training protocol for corpus comparison (1.3 B model, 150 B tokens)
Downstream benchmark suite and few‑shot CoT prompting
Results: performance gains, learning curves, multilingual impact
Key takeaways on size vs. quality

outline.description: Details the continual pre‑training process that yields the base model, including data mix, hyper‑parameters, and computational setup.
subtopics: Model initialization from DeepSeek‑Coder‑Base‑v1.5
Data mixture: math corpus, AlgebraicStack, arXiv, code, natural language
Training schedule, optimizer settings, batch size, learning‑rate schedule
Scaling to 500 B tokens: hardware and memory considerations

outline.chapter_title: Assessing Mathematical Capabilities of the Base Model
outline.description: Analyzes DeepSeekMath‑Base on a wide range of tasks: step‑by‑step reasoning, program‑aided solving, formal theorem proving, and general language/coding benchmarks.
subtopics: Few‑shot Chain‑of‑Thought evaluation on GSM8K, MATH, CMATH, etc.
Program‑of‑Thought (PoT) evaluation with Python tool use
Informal‑to‑formal proof generation on miniF2F/Isabelle
General NLP benchmarks (MMLU, BBH) and coding benchmarks (HumanEval, MBPP)
Impact of math pre‑training on non‑math abilities

outline.description: Explains how the base model is fine‑tuned on curated instruction data covering CoT, PoT, and tool‑integrated reasoning in both English and Chinese.
subtopics: Construction of the 776 K instruction dataset
Balancing chain‑of‑thought, program‑of‑thought, and tool‑integrated examples
Training regimen (tokens per batch, learning rate, context length)
Evaluation of DeepSeekMath‑Instruct vs. state‑of‑the‑art open‑source and closed models

outline.description: Introduces the RL stage, motivates it, and presents the novel Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) algorithm.
subtopics: Why RL after SFT improves reasoning (mis‑alignment, distribution sharpening)
Recap of Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) and its limitations for LLMs
Derivation of GRPO: group‑wise baseline, advantage estimation, KL regularization
Outcome vs. process supervision in GRPO
Iterative GRPO with reward‑model updates

outline.description: Covers the practical RL training pipeline, hyper‑parameters, and the performance boost obtained on both in‑domain and out‑of‑domain benchmarks.
subtopics: RL data selection (GSM8K & MATH questions only)
Reward model training and replay mechanism
Sampling strategy (64 outputs per question, batch size, max length)
Quantitative results: GSM8K, MATH, CMATH, MMLU‑STEM, BBH, etc.
Ablation studies: G‑size, KL coefficient, outcome vs. process

outline.chapter_title: Unified Paradigm for Fine‑Tuning and RL Methods
outline.description: Provides a theoretical framework that unifies SFT, RFT, DPO, PPO, and GRPO, and discusses empirical insights derived from this view.
subtopics: General gradient formulation and three components (data source, reward, algorithm)
Classification of methods: online vs. offline data, rule‑based vs. model‑based reward
Experimental comparison: online RFT vs. offline RFT, GRPO vs. PPO
Interpretation of why GRPO’s gradient coefficients are more effective
Iterative RL benefits and diminishing returns

outline.description: Summarizes empirical findings on data selection, code pre‑training, and arXiv usage, offering guidance for future research.
subtopics: Impact of code pre‑training on math reasoning (two‑stage vs. mixed training)
Why arXiv papers offered little benefit in this setting
Tips for building high‑quality math corpora from web data
Scalability considerations: token count vs. model size

outline.description: Outlines open challenges and promising research avenues, especially around RL improvements and geometric/theorem‑proving abilities.
subtopics: Enhancing geometry and formal proof performance
Advanced sampling & tree‑search for RL exploration
Robust RL algorithms against noisy reward signals (weak‑to‑strong alignment)
Better reward‑model uncertainty handling and process rewards
Scaling to larger models and multilingual extensions

outline.description: Recaps the contributions of DeepSeekMath, its impact on the open‑source ecosystem, and the broader significance for mathematical AI.
subtopics: Performance summary across benchmarks
Key takeaways about data quality, code training, and GRPO
Implications for open‑source AI research
